title: Design System: ML Systems Field Guide

display.purpose: Names the page and its largest learning question.

headline.purpose: Introduces major conceptual bands and transitions.

title.purpose: Labels panels, proofs, lab sheets, and ledger groups.

body.purpose: Carries explanations and instructions at a long-session reading rhythm.

label.purpose: Marks lifecycle, control, and evidence metadata.

mono.purpose: Exposes equations, tensor shapes, values, paths, hashes, and deterministic output.

shadows.name: floating-proof-inspector
shadows.purpose: Lifts the desktop proof inspector above an execution trace; removed when the inspector stacks.

shadows.name: photo-probe-separation
shadows.purpose: Separates small notebook probe pins from varied photographic paper.

motion.name: smooth-document-scroll
motion.purpose: Preserves orientation when following local anchors in the learning sequence.

motion.name: report-score-update
motion.purpose: Makes report completeness changes perceptible without animating content.

components.css: .ds-rail-list { margin:0; padding:.25rem .6rem 1rem; list-style:none; background:var(--surface, #fff); font-family:var(--font-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-rail-list li { position:relative; } .ds-rail-list li + li::before { content:""; position:absolute; left:1.05rem; top:-.65rem; height:.75rem; width:1px; background:var(--rule, #c7cfcb); } .ds-rail-list a { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1rem 1fr; gap:.6rem; padding:.75rem .55rem; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:var(--radius-sm, 6px); color:var(--muted, #4f5b66); text-decoration:none; } .ds-rail-dot { width:.72rem; height:.72rem; margin-top:.18rem; border:2px solid var(--rule-strong, #8d9994); border-radius:50%; background:var(--surface, #fff); } .ds-rail-list strong, .ds-rail-list small { display:block; } .ds-rail-list strong { font-size:.82rem; } .ds-rail-list small { margin-top:.1rem; color:var(--faint, #77838d); font-size:.68rem; } .ds-rail-list a:hover, .ds-rail-list a[aria-current="step"] { border-color:#a9bce9; color:var(--ink, #111418); background:var(--probe-soft, #e2ebff); } .ds-complete .ds-rail-dot, .ds-rail-list a[aria-current="step"] .ds-rail-dot { border-color:var(--probe, #1557d6); background:var(--probe, #1557d6); } .ds-rail-list a:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--amber, #f2c84b); outline-offset:3px; }

components.css: .ds-notebook-probe { position:relative; width:2.5rem; height:2.5rem; padding:0; border:0; background:transparent; cursor:pointer; } .ds-notebook-probe::before { content:""; position:absolute; top:50%; left:50%; width:1.15rem; height:1.15rem; border:3px solid var(--surface, #fff); border-radius:50%; background:var(--probe, #1557d6); box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(17,20,24,.25); transform:translate(-50%,-50%); } .ds-notebook-probe::after { content:attr(data-index); position:absolute; top:50%; left:calc(50% + .85rem); min-width:1.1rem; padding:.1rem .25rem; color:var(--surface, #fff); background:var(--probe, #1557d6); transform:translateY(-50%); font-family:var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size:.58rem; } .ds-notebook-probe[aria-pressed="true"]::before { width:1.45rem; height:1.45rem; border-radius:32%; background:var(--amber, #f2c84b); } .ds-notebook-probe:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--amber, #f2c84b); outline-offset:3px; }

components.css: .ds-report-ledger { border:1px solid var(--rule, #c7cfcb); color:var(--ink, #111418); background:var(--surface, #fff); font-family:var(--font-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-report-ledger summary { display:grid; grid-template-columns:2.2rem minmax(0,1fr) auto; gap:.75rem; align-items:center; min-height:4rem; padding:.75rem 1rem; cursor:pointer; list-style:none; } .ds-report-ledger summary::after { content:"+"; color:var(--probe, #1557d6); font-family:var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size:1.2rem; } .ds-report-ledger[open] summary::after { content:"−"; } .ds-ledger-index { display:grid; place-items:center; width:2rem; height:2rem; border:1px solid var(--probe, #1557d6); color:var(--probe, #1557d6); font-family:var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size:.72rem; } .ds-report-ledger strong, .ds-report-ledger small { display:block; } .ds-report-ledger small { margin-top:.18rem; color:var(--muted, #4f5b66); font-size:.7rem; } .ds-ledger-body { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:.9rem; padding:1rem; border-top:1px solid var(--rule, #c7cfcb); } .ds-ledger-body label { display:grid; gap:.32rem; font-size:.76rem; font-weight:650; } .ds-ledger-body em { margin-left:.35rem; padding:.08rem .3rem; border:1px solid #c6a62e; color:#725b00; background:var(--amber-soft, #fff5c9); font:500 .58rem/1.3 var(--font-mono, monospace); text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-ledger-body input { min-height:2.55rem; padding:.5rem .6rem; border:1px solid var(--rule-strong, #8d9994); border-radius:var(--radius-sm, 6px); color:var(--ink, #111418); background:var(--surface, #fff); font:400 1rem/1.55 var(--font-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-ledger-body input:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--amber, #f2c84b); outline-offset:3px; } @media (max-width:720px) { .ds-ledger-body { grid-template-columns:1fr; } }

narrative.overview:
Pipeline Debugger treats learning like stepping through a compiler and GPU trace. The visual system is a light, matte instrument deck: notebook-blue probes select inspectable claims; hairline rules expose boundaries; and dense but orderly panels keep equations, code trails, controls, and evidence visible together. It is technical without impersonating a terminal and pedagogical without turning the learner's handwriting into decoration.

The task-led hybrid changes composition without changing identity. Trace-first model pages, the notebook-first source decoder, browser-local lab sheets, and the ledger-first report builder all share the same utility strip, lifecycle rail, status language, panel anatomy, and proof-oriented interaction. The interface should feel calm enough for a long study session and exact enough that a learner can tell what is sourced, computed, illustrative, missing, or form-complete at a glance.
keyCharacteristics: Matte, light instrument surfaces separated by one-pixel diagnostic rules.
Cobalt probe pins and synchronized selection states derived from the notebook's blue dots.
Compact sans-serif hierarchy with monospace reserved for equations, paths, values, and machine output.
Evidence strength communicated by text and structure as well as color.
Responsive, printable, keyboard-operable layouts that retain the learning sequence.

tokenNotes.microType: 0.58rem–0.92rem is an intentional utility range for dense matrices, chips, probe indices, inline trace metadata, plot legends, and mono console output; never primary reading copy.
tokenNotes.tonalColors: Literal screen-specific blues, softened borders, and alert-border blends are members of the sidecar tonal ramps rather than additional semantic colors.
tokenNotes.shapeExceptions: 4px is the compact-control radius; 999px is the semantic-chip capsule radius. Instrument panels remain square.

rules.name: The Probe Is an Action Rule
rules.body: Cobalt marks something the learner can select, inspect, follow, or verify; never scatter it as ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Evidence Is Redundant Rule
rules.body: Every green, amber, red, or blue state repeats its meaning in a label, icon/dot, border, pattern, or status sentence so hue is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Sans-serif explains the system; monospace exposes the artifact. Do not use mono merely to make the site look technical.

rules.name: The Trace Survives Collapse Rule
rules.body: Responsive changes may stack or horizontally scroll dense structures, but they must preserve stage order, labels, current state, and the textual conclusion.

rules.name: The Linear Fallback Rule
rules.body: Every canvas, photo overlay, state matrix, or interactive plot needs a readable sequence, table, inspector, or output sentence in the document flow.

rules.name: The Flat Instrument Rule
rules.body: Cards, ledgers, labs, tables, and controls remain flat at rest; shadow is reserved for spatially floating evidence or pins over imagery.

rules.name: The Nearly Square Rule
rules.body: Apply rounding to controls and compact semantic chips, not to the instrument deck itself.

rules.name: The Evidence Boundary Rule
rules.body: Primary/official, verified-in-checkout, illustrative/needs-verification, and contradiction-required are source-quality states; intended-to-released is execution maturity. Never merge the two scales or let a strong source label imply that a run was executed.

dos: Do preserve the Pipeline Debugger metaphor by connecting every probe to an equation, code or source trail, observable consequence, and evidence task.
Do use cobalt only for current, inspectable, or repo-grounded state and repeat every status in words.
Do keep controls semantic and keyboard-operable, with visible amber focus, aria-current/aria-pressed state, labeled textual outputs, concise live feedback, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep prose near the 72ch measure while allowing tables, traces, images, and plots to use the wider instrument canvas.
Do label synthetic curves, browser-local calculations, missing artifacts, and external-system boundaries at the point of use.
Do maintain the print and linear-reading path when adding interaction.
donts: Don't round instrument panels, ledgers, lab sheets, or banners into generic soft cards.
Don't add decorative gradients, glows, or shadows; the grid paper, rules, and one floating inspector already establish depth.
Don't use monospace for ordinary explanation or cobalt as general decoration.
Don't turn notebook handwriting, blue dots, equations, or status lights into texture detached from a learning action.
Don't hide evidence state, source authority, or textual conclusions at narrow widths.
Don't imply that an illustrative visualization, configured script, or browser calculation is a measured training or serving run.
